featured_reviews.name: Josh
featured_reviews.review_text:
***Update***:

After I posted this review, the clinic responded publicly by denying any wrongdoing and implying that I was “getting too personal.” Instead of acknowledging the concern raised by a loyal client of 7+ years, they chose to deflect and subtly caution me against speaking up.

You can see their full response in the screenshot I’ve attached.

I am disappointed, but not surprised, by the clinic’s response — which avoided addressing any specific concern I raised and instead focused on defending their image. What’s more troubling is the subtle warning in their closing remark, implying that I should “be careful” not to “malign the character” of a lady veterinarian.

For the record, my review is based on documented personal experience, not character assassination. Describing a professional’s behaviour — especially after years of respectful patience — is not defamation, it is feedback. This is not a gender issue; it’s a professionalism issue.

Additionally, I did attempt to resolve the matter respectfully. My mother even sent a polite email, which was ignored. The claim that no opportunity was given is false.

Their unwillingness to acknowledge facts and their subtle attempt to silence criticism only reinforces the core problem: a lack of accountability and an inability to accept genuine feedback.

***Original review***

Based on my personal experience, I found this doctor’s behaviour to be rude and unprofessional. I no longer feel safe recommending this clinic to others.

Rude and Unprofessional Vet – Extremely Disappointing After 7 Years of Loyalty

I have been bringing my pet to this clinic for over 7 years, hoping that professionalism and empathy would eventually reflect in the doctor’s behaviour. Unfortunately, that has not been the case.

This vet consistently displays a rude, condescending, and dismissive attitude towards pet owners. Even when asking basic and important questions about the treatment being provided, I was met with irritation, raised voices, and an unwillingness to explain calmly. There is a clear lack of patience and emotional regulation, which creates an unsafe and uncomfortable experience for the pet’s family.

At times, it has felt as though she expects clients to stay silent and unquestioning — almost as if she’s doing us a favour rather than providing a paid, professional service. When I finally spoke up about the tone and manner in which I was being treated, her response was unapologetic. In her own words:

“Others have also told me I’m rude. I won’t apologise.”

That response was the final straw. To me, it reflected not just poor communication but a lack of accountability — something that is essential in any profession that involves care, trust, and emotional sensitivity.

Being a skilled vet does not excuse disrespectful behaviour towards people. Professional competence and basic human decency must go hand in hand. No amount of experience, money, or reputation can substitute that.

I was a loyal client for many years, but I no longer feel safe or respected at this clinic. I sincerely hope that the vet reflects on this and takes responsibility for the way clients are treated. If there is any meaningful apology or change in conduct in the future, I will update this review accordingly.

We are genuinely surprised and disappointed by your review, especially after over 7 years of consistent care provided to your pet. We have always made every effort to offer professional, honest, and thorough veterinary service.
While we understand that not every interaction will meet everyone's expectations, we firmly stand by the integrity of our work and our commitment to the well-being of our patients. Our clinic takes feedback seriously, but we do not accept personal attacks or misrepresentation of our intentions or behaviour.
If there was a specific concern regarding your pets health, you felt was not addressed appropriately, we would have appreciated the opportunity to resolve it at the same time. Nonetheless, we wish you and your pet well and thank you for the years you entrusted us with their care.

featured_reviews.name: John Paulraj
featured_reviews.review_text:
I heard about Dr. Pethe's Clinic when I had lost all hope.
Muthu was diagnosed of Acute Kidney Failure (creatinine 14.1) and my regular Vet was unable to do anything - that is when I visited the Pethes for a second opinion.
The Clinic is a very simple set up. But the people who take care of the place are Excellent!
Right from the very first day, when I watched how they were able to get Muthu's X-rays, and how they would literally treat him at his comfort level (meaning, they could tell that he was anxious and did their best to calm him - in fact, many times, they were on the floor when they had to give him an injection).
As a result of their never-giving-up-attitude, Muthu's creatine level dropped to 2.1 (in 3 months). For me, those 3 months were God-given days to cherish. Even though he was on medicines every day, even though we had to keep him on a strict diet and make regular visits to the Clinic, I am ever grateful to God for those 3 months. And, a huge reason for this are Dr. & Mrs. Pethe and all their staff.
Dogs can sense hospitals. Muthu would usually throw a tantrum whenever we approached the "super speciality pet hospital" which we were so accustomed to before we met the Pethes. But ever since we started going to Pethe's Clinic, Muthu became cooperative. I am sure the procedure was not easy on him either. But, he could tell that the people attending to him cared for him. You see, animals can tell by the touch - by the way we approach them. And Muthu was able to cooperate only because of the friendly and caring nature demonstrated by all the staff (Shinu, Ajay, and the others). They would give him biscuits, play with him, and make him feel comfortable. They didn't need people holding him down whenever they gave him bottles of saline (which would often last for 1.2 hours).
But even as Muthu's creatinine levels decreased, Dr & Mrs. Pethe were honest with me about his condition. And they did it with utmost care, concern, and compassion. They let me know that kidney failure could not be reversed.
After nearly 3.5 months of treatment, Muthu's condition began to worsen. And even during our last visit to the Clinic, Mrs. Pethe brought a 2 month pup near Muthu to make him smile.
It's been 6 months since I have lost my friend Muthu. And all pet lovers will know that it is not easy.
But, I am so glad to have met the Pethes who cared for him and helped me through those days.
Both Dr. & Mrs. Pethe are geniuses in their own way of knowledge and expertise.  But, what makes them stand out from the rest is their human touch and their genuine love and care for animals.
God bless the Team at Pethe's Clinic.

featured_reviews.name: Aishwarya Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
No More a Good Vet!!!

We have been bringing our kitty here for the past 7 years, but I am extremely disappointed with the lack of professionalism and medical skill shown.

My cat had developed a blood and kidney infection, to which the vet simply said:
1.	“Nothing to worry about.”
2.	Refused to take a blood test, claiming it wasn’t possible because my cat was paralysed and blood could not be drawn from her legs.

This negligence worsened her infection drastically. Instead of identifying the actual problem, the vet kept blaming her age – she is just 9 years old.

When I finally took her to Vetic Care, the new vet immediately conducted a blood test without any issue, diagnosed the condition in the first instant, and was shocked to hear what had been said before. Thanks to timely treatment, she is now recovering.

It is frustrating that years of trust ended in such unprofessional handling. The delay and misdiagnosis could have cost my kitty her life.

Incident 2 – A Local Cat
In another case, my mom had taken a local cat here for treatment. A blood sample was drawn, but when we asked for the report, the vet denied it, saying: “Blood kaam liya tha, test run hi nahi hua. Aap aake leke jao paise.” Basically, she kept the money and refused to provide any test results. That poor cat tragically died soon after.

The 4.5 stars now needs to be reduced… this is ridiculous

#patheticvet #noskills

featured_reviews.name: vikas nalawade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review about a stray cat named “Leopard” who eventually became our family member. Request you to please read it till end, as it may be helpful to any pet parent.
Leopard met with an accident and was missing for a week’s period. Later we found him & we noticed that he had a fracture at shoulder of right forelimb. Doctors told us that leg needs to be operated by inserting rod in his leg, so we got him operated by Dr. Sunetra. The surgery went well, but three days after surgery, Leopard's operated leg started swelling, we informed Dr. Sunetra but she told us it is the swelling due to surgery and it will subside downwards. But that swelling was due to infection and it lead to pus formation. Next day the swelling increased and in the evening pus started oozing out, seeing this we called up Dr. Sunetra & rushed to her with our Leopard. Dr. told us to keep flushing the wound twice a day with betadine. After 2-3 days of this treatment, the skin around the infected area went dead and we had a clear sight of his wound with operated area, where we could see his bone from two points because healing was not completed & the stitches were opened. We even asked Dr. Sunetra the doubt in our mind that this infection will not spread in his operated leg & internal body, to which she responded, it would not.
Eventually his external pain reduced but he had internal pain, which we failed to understand. He could not tolerate the pain and stopped eating and got fever exactly on 8th day from operation. We informed this situation of Leopard at every visit to Dr. Sunetra, but she recommended to force feed our Leopard. Later on our Leopard left with no energy to walk on his own and lift his neck, he even started heavy breathing. After informing this situation to Dr. Sunetra, she then advised us to put saline for his recovery but nowhere had she conveyed that Leopard’s health is deteriorating & he needs hospitalization. At this time, she was going out of town & was not available for 4-5 days.
Since, Dr. Sunetra was not available, we went to other Vet doctor who knew Leopard's medical history. This doctor told us to continue saline treatment twice a day for at least 4-5 days. Here the blood test was also done to examine the condition of our Leopard, where the report came with alarming & critical output depicting WBC increased & Platelets dropped to severe condition. Even this doctor also not recommended that our Leopard require hospitalization. This was the 11th day after operation.
The 12th day story (i.e. 1st July 23) of our Leopard was worst. The morning session of his saline was completed & even this second doctor went out of town for 3-4 days without recommending hospitalization. By evening, somewhere from 4:30pm, the heavy breathing became worse & we could not see his pain. We started calling Dr. Sunetra, but her phone was not reachable, so we text her on WhatsApp along with Leopard’s blood report. Since no response from doctor, with Leopard, we rushed to a Vet hospital, where he was admitted with a note by the doctors, like heavy breathing & drop in body temperature, which was very critical condition. He was kept in ICU incubator with oxygen supply to ease his breathe & improve his body temperature. The hospital doctors even told us that there are chances that the infection might have spread into blood. Unfortunately battling with pain & breathing problem our Leopard passed away on the same day around 11 pm.
There are certain questions for Dr. Sunetra;
# Why you haven't included any medicine for infection post-surgery?
# Why you did not advised us prior to start saline, when we informed you that Leopard lost his appetite?
# Why you did not look closely if the infection was spreading in the body? If you think it wasn't then why did he lost his appetite, had weakness, got fever, started heavy breathing?
# Why you took everything so lightly and casually in his case? Was it because it was a stray cat?

The doctor’s entire focus was on the operated area and the wound & the rest health parameters were ignored completely.

Extremely Disappointing Experience at Vetic Borivali (IC Colony)

I had a very bad and frustrating experience at the Vetic clinic in Borivali IC Colony while treating my dog for a bite wound.

On the first visit, the doctor on duty examined my dog and advised me to clean the wound with Savlon and apply Placentrex gel using a syringe for a few days. I carefully followed the exact instructions at home for the entire duration prescribed because I didn’t want to risk my dog getting infected.

When we returned for a follow-up after a few days, a different doctor attended us — Dr. Abhijeet Vishwas Yadav. He suggested adding another ointment to the treatment. I politely explained that I preferred to continue the same treatment plan the first doctor had given because changing the routine midway might make the wound worse or cause infection.

Instead of explaining calmly, he responded very rudely and arrogantly, saying, “I’m the doctor here. You listen to me or go to the previous doctor in the Kandivali branch.” Despite the tone, I stayed calm and eventually followed the instructions he gave.

However, after following those instructions — cleaning the wound more with Savlon and applying the gel — my dog’s condition actually became worse. The wound started swelling, a large amount of pus started coming out, and my dog even stopped eating because of the pain.

Today we had another follow-up appointment and unfortunately I had to meet the same doctor again. I explained that after following the treatment suggested, my dog’s wound had gotten worse. Instead of checking the situation properly, he immediately blamed me and said it was my fault and not his.

That response was extremely frustrating. As a pet owner, why would I randomly change treatments given by doctors from the same clinic? I was simply following the instructions provided.

Dr. Abhijeet Vishwas Yadav was extremely rude, dismissive, and disrespectful throughout the interaction. His attitude showed no empathy toward the animal or the concerned pet owner. At one point he even said that if I wasn’t satisfied I could take my dog somewhere else.

To make matters worse, the receptionist was also extremely rude. When I tried to explain the situation, he casually said that I could “file a case or do whatever I want” and that they didn’t care. Such behavior from clinic staff is completely unacceptable.

A veterinary clinic should show compassion, professionalism, and responsibility — especially when dealing with worried pet owners and injured animals. Unfortunately, my experience here was the complete opposite.

Please don’t take your pets to this Vetic clinic if you truly care about their health and well-being. My experience here was extremely disappointing and unprofessional from both the doctor and the staff.

Review for Pet Clinic Gorai – Dr. Premal Darji

I am writing this with extreme pain after losing my beloved pet, Erika.

I was referred to Pet Clinic Gorai and trusted Dr. Premal Darji completely. That trust has turned into lifelong regret.

Erika had a tumor case, and instead of receiving clear surgical direction and decisive medical planning, her treatment kept getting prolonged with medications. During this period, her condition worsened, and she started experiencing severe bleeding episodes.

We repeatedly requested clarity about surgical intervention and long-term treatment planning. However, we never received firm guidance or urgency that such a critical case required.

At one stage, her platelet levels dropped significantly, and her bleeding became uncontrollable. Watching your pet lose blood helplessly while depending on professional guidance is something no pet parent should ever experience. Despite multiple visits and continuous follow-ups, her condition deteriorated rapidly.

We were left confused, emotionally shattered, and without clear answers.

If you are dealing with a serious or tumor-related condition, please:
– Ask for detailed blood reports and explanations
– Ask about platelet monitoring
– Seek immediate second opinions
– Do not delay critical decisions

Blind trust in medical situations can cost you everything. In our case, it cost us our family member.

featured_reviews.name: Jonita Quadras
featured_reviews.review_text:
We rescued our cat, Kiki, on January 29th 2025. A couple of weeks in, we suspected she might be pregnant and took her to Dr. Premal Darji. He strongly advised immediate spaying, assuring us it was completely safe and routine. Trusting his judgment, we went ahead with the surgery.

Soon after, Kiki began vomiting excessively — far more than what he described as “normal.” She stopped eating, peeing, or pooping. We visited his clinic daily post-op, but Dr. Darji had no clear answers. At one point, he even said he hadn’t “seen a case like this before,” but never recommended a specialist or second opinion.

Eventually, when we visited another vet, bloodwork revealed that Kiki’s creatinine was dangerously high (15) — a clear sign of acute kidney failure. We went back to Dr. Darji for an ultrasound, but again he insisted that “everything looked fine,” and failed to identify the actual issue. Even then, he didn’t show any urgency or transparency in managing the situation.

Desperate for help, we rushed her to Top Dog Clinic in Andheri, where they quickly diagnosed that urine was leaking into her abdomen, most likely due to trauma caused during the original spay surgery. They couldn’t keep her overnight, so we stabilized her at Blue 7 Vets in Borivali, and the next day, Top Dog performed a critical, life-saving surgery.

Kiki thankfully made it through, and while she still has one more surgery to go, she’s finally recovering. What’s most upsetting is that none of this had to happen. Dr. Darji never took accountability or gave us the information we needed to act sooner. His lack of proper communication and judgment not only endangered Kiki’s life but also left us emotionally drained and over ₹2 lakhs deep in treatment costs that could have been avoided.

This isn’t to spread hate, but to create awareness. If you feel unsure or uncomfortable with your vet’s advice, please don’t hesitate to seek a second opinion. Your pet’s life and your peace of mind are worth it.

I am reporting this to relevant authorities as Vetic wants to shield the negligence.

Formal Complaint: Negligence in Post-Operative Care Resulting in Death of Cat – Indra (01.01.2025)
I am writing this email with deep grief and distress to formally report negligence and lack of due medical care by your veterinarian at Vetic Kandivali, which resulted in the death of my cat, Indra.

On 01.01.2025, I brought Indra, a free-roaming cat under my care, to your Kandivali clinic as he was bleeding from the mouth. After examination, your veterinarian diagnosed that Indra’s teeth were broken and decayed and advised that dental extraction was required. The procedure was carried out at your clinic.

Post-procedure, Indra was safely kept in a cage at his usual location for observation. However, he bled excessively through the night. Early the next morning, I immediately brought Indra back to the same veterinarian and showed him clear photographs evidencing significant blood loss from the mouth.

Despite being presented with visible proof of continuous bleeding after a dental procedure, the veterinarian stated that he “could not see any bleeding points” in the mouth and took no corrective or preventive action. No emergency intervention, no saline support, no observation, and no admission for monitoring was advised or initiated. Indra was sent back with me.

Within approximately one hour of returning, Indra began bleeding again. I immediately called the same veterinarian and informed him that the bleeding had resumed. At this point, instead of addressing the emergency himself, he advised me to consult another veterinarian from the same clinic chain, stating that a senior doctor there “might be more competent.”

This statement itself is alarming. If the treating veterinarian believed he was not competent to handle a post-operative complication, he should have escalated the matter immediately in the morning itself, retained the cat under observation, or ensured emergency stabilisation. Sending a bleeding animal away without monitoring or intervention amounts to gross negligence.

Due to the failure to act in time and the lack of appropriate post-operative care, Indra continued to bleed and ultimately passed away.

I request the following from your end within 7 days of receipt of this email:

A complete written explanation of the diagnosis, dental procedure performed, and post-operative assessment.

Clarification on why no emergency measures or observation were initiated despite clear signs of blood loss.

Details of the veterinarian(s) involved, including qualifications and roles.

Please note that this email is being sent as a formal record. In the absence of a satisfactory response, I will be constrained to escalate this matter to the State Veterinary Council, Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, and other appropriate authorities for negligence and deficiency in service.

This communication is written in pain, but also with the expectation of accountability from a professional medical establishment.

Sincerely,

featured_reviews.name: sms sweta
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a pet parent, I’m sure many of you will understand the kind of fear and helplessness we feel when something isn’t right with our baby. I went through exactly that when my 14-year-old feline, Goldie, was diagnosed with a serious tumour on her left paw. Those days were filled with worry, questions, and uncertainty.

All we knew was that we needed the right oncologist — someone we could trust completely. That’s when we found the incredible team at Superpets, and from that very first visit, everything began to feel a little lighter.

From explaining the diagnosis and possible causes, to guiding us through every test, every step was handled with so much patience, clarity, and compassion. What truly stood out was how reassuring the entire team was — always available to answer questions, clear doubts, and take that extra effort to make both us and Goldie feel comfortable.

The journey — from diagnosis, to surgery, to post-operative care and stitch removal — was smoother than we could have ever hoped for. Every decision they made felt right, thoughtful, and in Goldie’s best interest.

A special note of gratitude to Dr. Pratyush, Dr. Vasudha, and Dr. Gauri — you are truly angels in disguise. The care, dedication, and gentleness with which you handled Goldie means the world to us. It’s not just medical expertise, but your genuine love for animals that makes all the difference.

I must admit, I was initially skeptical about traveling all the way from the suburbs to Bandra for treatment — but today, I can say with complete conviction that every visit, every effort, was absolutely worth it.

What touched me deeply was that even after a month, Dr. Pratyush personally followed up to check on Goldie’s health. That level of care is rare and speaks volumes about the kind of people they are — not just doctors, but true lifesavers.

This entire experience has been a journey of gratitude. People like them are not just treating animals — they are healing families.

Thank you, Superpets team, from the bottom of my heart, for taking such beautiful care of our baby.

Forever grateful. 🙏🏻

featured_reviews.name: Smitaa Nair
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is a blessing. My German shepherd champ was taken to super pets in an emergency situation. He had developed something called GDV. I was unaware if this situation being a pet parent since more than 17 years now (I have had pets since several years) After taking him to vetic hospital for emergency (which was extremely careless and didn’t even treat it like emergency) post his X-ray on recommendation from some friends I rushed him to super pets. They immediately took charge of the situation. He underwent operation and was discharged in 5 days. We had to take him for regular follow ups and on a follow up in a weeks time, doctors suspected something wrong and again on further tests discovered that his spleen had got affected and damaged along with few further conditions that had developed. He underwent second surgery. He battled for his life for a month in this hospital. He was hospitalised. The care, affection and love he recieved along with the proper medical care is nothing less than a gift for parents seeing their child fight for life and death each day. Inspite of he being aggressive he was pampered and taken care of as if he belongs to them. His entire body had collapsed and post 1 month he finally got discharged. He had lost his ability to walk post all this condition as his hip and spine had got affected. We continued Physio with them. It’s October today. My boy got discharged in June and we are in our way for our regular Physio all hail and hearty, not just walking but running and bullying my other 2 dogs :) No words can thank them enough. His recovery is nothing less than a miracle only because of timely care and attention given to him by the super vets at super pets.
